en: Now, before we dive into this messy code I
showed you and before we will start cleaning
it up,
let me give you an overview over the various
techniques and rules which we have when it
comes to cleaning up control structures.
Because of course, an important part of
using control structures in a clean way is
that you avoid deep nesting.
To achieve this, we can use factory
functions and polymorphism, And we'll of
course see what exactly that is and how it
helps us.
You can also tweak your
naming or the way you formulate your if
checks a little bit. And for example, prefer
positive checks over negative checks
because positive checks are
typically a bit easier to understand.
And you can also utilize errors and not just
see them as a problem, but instead use them
in a smart way to get rid of certain if
checks which you don't need actually.
Of course, the composition and polymorphism
and the error part here will also be
important tools when it comes to achieving
the main goal of avoiding deep nesting.
Now, these are all concepts we're going to
have a look at throughout this course
section, but I will actually start with a
different concept, guards.
